title: How beavers reshape entire river ecosystems

scenes.narration: In Europe, beavers were reduced to fragmented populations, with combined population numbers being estimated across multiple river basins.
Beavers live in freshwater ecosystems such as rivers, streams, lakes and ponds across their native geographic distribution ranges.
The concept became popular in conservation, and was deployed in a range of contexts to engender support for protecting habitats.
Human activities had damaged ecosystems, such as by removing keystone predators that previously maintained balance in those natural environments.
In addition, wolves often kept animals from grazing in riparian areas, which protected beavers from having their food sources encroached upon.
The connectivity of streams to their adjacent floodplain along their entire length plays an important role in the equilibrium of the river system.
Stream restoration or river restoration, sometimes called river reclamation in the United Kingdom, is a set of activities that aim to improve environmental health.
However, it is important to note that these groups do not cover the entire range known to be occupied by the subspecies today.
